## Review
`Lady Dua` is a thriller that depicts the cat-and-mouse suspense between a woman who wanted to become a perfect luxury item, even if fake, and a detective who relentlessly pursues the truth she holds.  

It sharply delves into heavy questions about `truth` by exploiting the <mark>vanity and desire</mark> hidden within modern people.  

As the truth is uncovered, her identity is gradually revealed, and the desires and psychology of the characters that emerge in the process are intriguing.  
It's impressive how she knows exactly what her targets want and uses that to achieve her own goals.  

I liked the way the relationships between characters gradually expanded and intertwined, eventually converging into a single truth.  

Even she, who plans everything meticulously, is shown to be shaken by the unexpected madness of a certain human being.  

Her final choice provides an answer to whether she truly loves her brand or merely used it for her own desires.  

The acting of the protagonists was overwhelming.  
Shin Hye-sun perfectly portrayed the inner self of a captivating yet dangerous character whose thoughts are impossible to read, while Lee Jun-hyuk also delivered a multi-dimensional performance as he fiercely pursues her while falling into confusion.

"Can it be fraud if there are no victims coming forward?"  
"Can it be considered fake if it's indistinguishable from the real thing?"
